fluff.overview:
The Hoplite was introduced in 2578 by Martinson Armaments of Terra as an infantry support BattleMech for the newly formed Star League Defense Force. Entering service during the opening battles of the Reunification War, the fifty-five-ton design proved itself a capable fire support platform, pairing a heavy autocannon with a long-range missile launcher to provide covering fire for advancing infantry formations. After a failed attempt to create a mainline combat variant, Martinson upgraded the electronics suite to produce the HOP-4C, though the design was ultimately relegated to Terran Hegemony militia commands by the twenty-seventh century.

Thought lost during the Amaris Crisis and early Succession Wars, the Hoplite survived among the SLDF exiles who would become the Clans, where its simple and rugged construction made it ideal for rapid production. The design later reappeared in the Inner Sphere in the hands of Wolf's Dragoons, raising immediate questions about the mercenary command's mysterious origins.
fluff.capabilities:
Intended to operate in close coordination with infantry, the Hoplite sacrifices speed for firepower and protection. Its DAV 220 engine provides a maximum speed of only sixty-four kilometers per hour, making it one of the slower medium 'Mechs in service, but eleven and a half tons of DuraShield armor give it impressive staying power for its weight class. The primary armament of the HOP-4D centers on a Mydron Excel LB 10-X autocannon, capable of firing both standard and cluster ammunition, providing tactical flexibility against both hardened and dispersed targets. A Conan/5 LRM-5 launcher supplements the autocannon with long-range indirect fire capability, though the modest missile load requires careful ammunition management.

The Hoplite's design philosophy emphasizes reliability over sophistication. Sixteen heat sinks provide more than adequate cooling for its weapons loadout, and the standard fusion engine ensures the 'Mech can absorb significant punishment without catastrophic failure. However, the lack of jump jets and limited speed make the Hoplite vulnerable to flanking maneuvers, reinforcing its doctrinal role as a support unit rather than a frontline combatant.
fluff.history:
The Hoplite's combat debut came against Taurian troops on Ridgebrook during the Reunification War, where its ability to absorb considerable punishment proved instrumental in anchoring SLDF infantry formations against determined Concordat counterattacks. Having demonstrated its effectiveness, the Hoplite became a common sight in 'Mech battalions assigned to infantry support roles throughout the conflict.

As the Reunification War dragged on, the SLDF's evolving tactical doctrine outpaced the Hoplite's capabilities. Increasingly advanced designs from the Terran Hegemony's factories saw the Hoplite redeployed alongside designs such as the Mackie and Banshee in Hegemony militia units, where it would suffer the heaviest casualties during the Rim Worlds Republic's seizure of the Terran Hegemony in the late twenty-eighth century. Martinson Armaments' factory on Terra was destroyed during the fighting in 2767, effectively ending Inner Sphere production.

The design survived among Aleksandr Kerensky's SLDF exiles, who valued its simplicity and ease of manufacture. When Nicholas Kerensky led his followers to Strana Mechty, the Hoplite blueprints were carried along, and an upgraded version (the HOP-4Bb) entered limited production at facilities on Strana Mechty and Eden in the years before the Pentagon Civil War. The Clans distributed the design among their toumans, though reactions varied considerably. The Snow Ravens rejected the Hoplite entirely due to its sluggish performance, while the Goliath Scorpions embraced its long-range capabilities.

Wolf's Dragoons selected the Hoplite for their journey to the Inner Sphere in 3005, believing the ancient design would avoid drawing attention. This calculation proved spectacularly wrong, as the appearance of a supposedly extinct 'Mech only deepened suspicions about the Dragoons' true origins. After cutting ties with the Clan Homeworlds in 3020, the Dragoons lost access to replacement Hoplites, and attrition steadily reduced their numbers. Following the Battle of Luthien in 3052, surviving Hoplites were refitted with salvaged Clan technology at Blackwell Corporation's facilities on Outreach, while experimental mixed-tech variants emerged from Arc-Royal MechWorks during the Jihad era.

By the Dark Age, Arc-Royal MechWorks had developed the HOP-5C, a cheap trooper variant using locally available materials to address Clan Jade Falcon's continued encroachment on the Arc-Royal Defense Cordon. Though never a prestigious design, the Hoplite's extraordinary longevity (spanning from the Reunification War through the ilClan era) stands as proof of the enduring value of simple, rugged engineering.
fluff.deployment: Developed exclusively for Wolf's Dragoons following the Battle of Luthien in 3052, the Hoplite C serves as a comprehensive refit using salvaged Clan technology. Ten tons of Clan ferro-fibrous armor replace the original DuraShield protection, while double heat sinks accommodate a significantly upgraded weapons suite. The primary armament is a Clan Ultra AC/10 supplemented by a Clan LRM-15 for long-range engagements, with three torso-mounted energy weapons (two medium pulse lasers and an extended-range medium laser) providing close-range firepower. The refit was performed at Blackwell Corporation's facilities on Outreach.
